In add_class_tvars, for a staticmethod (is_classmethod=False) with isuper present (C[int]), the tvars from isuper are NOT expanded. The fix: for static methods accessed on class, expand by isuper like classmethods do (but without binding self). Actually currently the CallableType branch only expands for classmethod. For staticmethod, `C[int].c` should expand T->int. But for `C.c` (bare), isuper would be C[T,S...]? map_instance_to_supertype of itype where itype is C[T] bare? When accessed as `C.c`, itype is... original_vars given. In that case tvars added make it generic def [T] () -> C[T], good. When `C[int].c`, original_vars empty and isuper=C[int]; we should expand.

Fix: in the CallableType branch:

elif isuper is not None:

entries.author: teacher
entries.content: Root cause: in `add_class_tvars` in `mypy/checkmember.py`, when a static method of a generic class was accessed on a parameterized class object (e.g. `C[int].c`), the method's signature was never expanded with the instance's type arguments — the `expand_type_by_instance(t, isuper)` call only happened for classmethods. As a result the return type kept the raw class type variable (`C[T]`) instead of the substituted one (`C[int]`), producing the confusing `got "C[T]", expected "C[T]"` error when the two type variables differed in identity. The fix adds an `elif isuper is not None: t = expand_type_by_instance(t, isuper)` branch so static methods also get their class type variables substituted; bare `C.c` access still yields a generic callable since the typevars are re-added via `original_vars`. Verified with the issue example, reveal_type checks, and relevant existing test suites (classes, generics, classmethod/staticmethod, overloading, protocols, typevar — all pass).
